turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The inverted (p-i-n) MAPbI3 stack requires a high-work-function, low-recombination HTL, a fullerene-based ETL that passivates the perovskite and extracts electrons, a thin wide-gap buffer (BCP/Bphen/PEI) that blocks holes and forms an ohmic cathode contact, and a chemically compatible metal (Cu or Ag). Film quality is highest for spin-coated absorbers on smooth ITO/FTO glass.

These constraints immediately highlight five pool entries whose layer combinations reproduce (or modestly improve upon) the highest-PCE training recipes:

- Au-np/NiO supplies both plasmonic absorption enhancement and a well-aligned p-contact (training analogue 20 %); the extra PEI dipole further lowers the cathode barrier.
- PTAA/PMMA is a proven low-recombination HTL (training analogue 19.5 %); the IDTT2FPDI/PCBM/Bphen stack adds complementary electron extraction and hole blocking.
- PTAA / PCBM/BCP / Cu is the canonical high-Voc inverted architecture; Cu minimises halide-metal reactions relative to Ag or Al.
- Li/Mg-doped NiO (NiMgLiO) was specifically engineered for conductivity and valence-band alignment; PCBM/BCP/Ag completes a low-loss cathode.
- P3CT-Na together with a C60/BCP bilayer reproduces the 18.5 % training cell that used the closely related ITCPTC-Th acceptor.

Flexible substrates, missing buffers, PEDOT:PSS, and purely evaporative or blade-coated films are all associated with 1–3 % absolute losses in the training set and are therefore excluded.

Final: c038, c030, c044, c041, c097
